content.title: About
content.content: Plain nonfat yogurt is a dairy product made by fermenting skim milk with live cultures of Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus. It has a mild creamy taste, very low fat (usually less than 0.5 %), and is rich in protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nonfat yogurt is a staple in many diet plans because of its low calorie density.
The live cultures support gut health by promoting beneficial bacteria.
In several countries it is traditionally served with honey, fresh berries, or nuts.
Fermentation reduces lactose, making it easier to digest for lactose‑intolerant individuals.
Nonfat yogurt is often used in cooking as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A typical 245 g serving provides about 10 g of protein, helping maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: It contains roughly 40–50 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Yogurt supplies about 15 % of the daily calcium requirement, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Probiotic cultures aid the growth of beneficial gut bacteria, improving digestion.

items.title: Very low fat
items.content: The nonfat version contains virtually no saturated fat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to yogurt.

items.title: Added sugars in some brands
items.content: Certain manufacturers add sugar or sweeteners, increasing the calorie count.

items.title: Probiotic viability may decline
items.content: Live cultures can decrease over time during refrigerated storage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yogurt can be eaten plain, blended into smoothies, used in sauces, dressings, baked goods, or as a base for dips. It pairs well with berries, fruit, nuts, and honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep yogurt refrigerated at 1–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
